correctness.rationale: In row sum/difference orthobasis the random update has diagonal entries 1-alpha p and 1-alpha r and off-diagonal -alpha sqrt(pr) xi with E xi=0, E xi^2=1/q. This closes expected squared-coordinate moments under the symmetric nonnegative T with entries ((1-alpha p)^2, alpha^2 pr/q, (1-alpha r)^2). Every nonzero deterministic initial squared-coordinate vector pairs strictly positively with the Perron eigenvector, making rho(T) necessary/sufficient. Independent exact-rational evaluations confirmed det(I-T)=alpha^2 pr[4-2alpha+alpha^2 pr(1-q^-2)] across c=1/3,3/5,5/13 and q=1,2,3,6, and confirmed the growth-but-convergence witness q=2,c=3/5,alpha=9/4: one-step gain 209/200 and det(I-T)=3483/40000. The two principal minors prove the global boundary. Mean-square rate is a strictly convex simple top eigenvalue; derivative sign changes between alpha=1 and alpha=2 give unique optimizer, with a perturbative Schur expansion as c approaches 1 giving the stated sqrt(1-c) coefficient. Finite evaluations supplement analytic exactness.

originality.rationale: Moorman et al define the same simultaneous averaged RK update; their theorem/corollary give a ONE-STEP spectral error guarantee, and its optimizer targets that guarantee. The inspected full author-hosted 2019 version does not give the two-row exact infinite-time Perron stability frontier, including stable transient expansion. Resultary hits concern cyclic Kaczmarz and greedy/coherence Kaczmarz, not the same independent uniform minibatch covariance. The general stochastic linear-system literature is broad; a spectral mean-square specialization remains possible but not demonstrated.
residual_risks: A general mean-square stochastic linear iteration result might imply this exact two-row spectral condition after specialization.
The fixed-q high-coherence expansion is not a uniform limit in q.
Additional 2020 journal version of Moorman et al was not read page-by-page in this run.

value.rationale: The sharp strict gap between guaranteed stepwise monotonicity and true long-run mean-square stability is a structural quantitative boundary for simultaneous row averaging; the exact rate optimizer and fixed-q near-coincident-row asymptotic are useful for tuning and for understanding transient amplification in a natural minimal correlated system.

final_claim: For two nonparallel unit rows of correlation c in (0,1), independent equally weighted minibatch size q>=1 and constant alpha>0, exact all-initial-condition mean-square convergence iff alpha<4/(1+sqrt(c^2+(1-c^2)/q^2)); one-step nonexpansion iff alpha<=4/(1+c+(1-c)/q). For q>1 these differ strictly. The Perron mean-square rate has a unique minimizer alpha* in (1,2), with its stated fixed-q high-coherence asymptotic.
limitations: Only real 2x2 consistent systems, two normalized nonparallel unit rows, unbiased independent row draws with replacement and fixed q.
Global mean-square criterion is not the per-iteration decrease criterion, and fastest rate is not finite-horizon optimum.
No claims for noisy, unequal, adaptive, asynchronous or more than two rows.
